messages:
sam.w: quick thought — propose we split slab ownership into two orthogonal layers: SlabCatalog (metadata + residency hints, read-only for fast path) and SlabController (leases, eviction policy, demote decisions). rationale: shrink lock surfaces on hot reads and move complex eviction coordination to controller. opinions?

maya: i like the separation. main worry: demotion visibility. readers must have a cheap way to know 'this prefix is demoted' without hitting controller on every op. maybe a generation counter on SlabCatalog?

roberto: generation counter + tag could work but watch GC and rollover. i'd prefer a short soft-lease that readers acquire at first access; controller only evicts once leases expire and a fence is observed. avoids global seqnums.

sam.w: fwiw soft-lease seems easier for correctness, counter is faster but harder to reason about with async handoffs. lease model: readers get lease token (ttl ~200ms). controller tries to revoke and waits for TTL + grace before hard-evict.

jen: quick proto sketch for the RPC boundary: ```proto
service SlabController {
  rpc Pin(PinReq) returns (PinResp); // get soft-lease
  rpc TryEvict(EvictReq) returns (EvictAck); // controller-driven
  rpc MarkDemote(MarkReq) returns (MarkAck); // hints for prefetcher
}
message PinReq { string prefix = 1; string requester = 2; }
```

kevin: minor nit: Pin on fast path needs to be local in most cases. please ensure SlabCatalog caches last-known lease-state so readers don't block on RPC for 95% cases. use async refresh.

maya: agree. SlabCatalog should be authoritative for last-observed state and also expose a cheap bitset for demoted/pinned flags. controller ops mutate catalog via a CAS. readers consult catalog -> if miss then fallback to controller pin RPC.

roberto: edgecase: two controllers (split brain) both think they can evict same slab. need a lease owner reconciliation. we already have node IDs in the runtime; controller should attach controller-epoch and sign evict requests. require at-most-one-winner via K-compare (epoch+id).

sam.w: good catch. add conflict resolution rule: highest (controller_epoch, node_id) wins; other side must backoff and re-sync catalog.

jen: tests we should add: 1) reader sees demote then read-after-demote still allowed until lease expiry, 2) simultaneous demote+pin race, 3) controller crash during eviction -> recovery walk re-checks catalog + active leases.

kevin: metrics to gate rollout: prefix-evict-failures, prefix-evict-retries, prefix-lease-contention, read-latency-p50/p99. also watch tenant-side 429s and token backpressure.

prefetch-bot: deploy-check: prefetcher-compatible=true, sticky-ttl=200ms, canary-sample=10%

maya: rollout plan: feature-flag off by default; opt-in per-cluster. start with non-critical small tenants, watch eviction-retries and read-latency for 48h, then expand. if prefix-evict-failures > 0.1% revert.

roberto: implementation note: keep SlabCatalog durable but compact. catalog entries should be small: prefix, residency_hint, last_generation_tag, pinned_count_hint. controller keeps decision logs for troubleshooting.

sam.w: open questions: 1) demote vs soft-evict naming (we should pick clear semantics), 2) whether controller should be sharded per-slab or per-tenant, 3) telemetry names.

kevin: naming: "soft-demote" = mark for eviction but allow existing leases to finish; "hard-evict" = reclaim immediately after grace. shard controller by tenant-id to reduce cross-tenant coordination.

jen: I'll draft an RFC appendix with the proto, invariants, and a small canary test harness (kitchen-sink scenarios + chaos injection). aim for next Wed review.

sam.w: great. can someone volunteer to own the canary plan? @kevin?

kevin: sure, i'll own canary plan. i'll put checklist in the RFC PR.

maya: i'll take the tests. i'll also write a small sim that models leases + eviction timing to sanity-check parameters.

roberto: i'll prototype controller sharding and conflict resolution sketch.

sam.w: thanks all — we're converging. dropping short list of action items in the RFC thread and will link tests + proto. :thumbsup:
